thread.title: Investors Not Giving Up On Tech Stocks Despite FAANG Woes

author: BLOOMBERG NEWS
title: Investors Not Giving Up On Tech Stocks Despite FAANG Woes
text:
Some experts are recommending shorting the FAANG bloc of tech stocks. But ETF investors are buying it – literally.
X State Street 's ( STT ) Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund ( XLK ) took in $725 million last week, the most since January 2017. And before an outflow of $244 million on Friday, the $23 billion fund was on its way to posting its highest weekly inflows ever.
The buying flies in the face of advice from Bank of America, where strategists led by Michael Hartnet included shorting Facebook ( FB ), Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google parent Alphabet ( GOOGL ) in a list of trades for the second half of 2018.
"Once again a posse of bears has surfaced predicting that this latest stumble in technology stocks could prove different than technology stocks' other misses earlier this year," John Stoltzfus, the chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co., wrote in a note to clients Monday. "With fundamentals pretty much intact among the names that stumbled last week, we'd be reluctant to get too bearish on technology."

That's still significantly less FAANG exposure than the $68 billion Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 ETF ( QQQ ), which has more than a quarter of its holdings in the group. QQQ saw a string of outflows last week, losing more than $1.4 billion.
XLK and QQQ, the two largest technology ETFs, do overlap on one stock: Both have Apple at the top of their lists. And with the company set to report earnings after Tuesday's market close, ETF investors will be eyeing these funds closely.
